messages:
carlos-cs: FYI Acme on-boarding hit us with a support ticket — embeddings endpoint latency spiked yesterday and today, vectors/sec dropping ~6x compared to baseline. customer says >100ms per vector -> impacting their realtime search. they provided sample request IDs.

sam-support: ack. can you paste the request IDs and a sample payload? any error codes from our API?

carlos-cs: request IDs: req_20260314_aa1, req_20260314_bb2. No 4xx errors, mostly 200s but responses are much slower. they sent batch of 128 inputs (each ~30 tokens). payload shape: documents:128, model: redwood-embed-v1. dims reported on client: 1024.

sam-support: thanks. two quick asks: 1) can they repro with smaller batch (e.g., 8) to see vectors/sec change? 2) can we get server-side telemetry for those request IDs (queue depth, gpu util)? I'll pull logs.

marta-sre: digging into infra metrics for those timestamps — I see a correlated bump in per-instance queue_depth on embed-pool-eu: queue depth went from ~6 to ~48 around 03:12 UTC. GPU util also jumped to 96% and stayed there for ~15m.

ryan-ml: that smells like batching/backpressure causing long tail. model redwood-embed-v1 had a quantized kernel change in last rollout (release 2026.3.12) that adjusted pack_batch heuristics. stepping through logs now for `req_20260314_aa1`.

sam-support: customer also reported intermittent shape mismatch warnings on client logs: `embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768 got 1024` — but they said vectors are being returned, just slower. could be that client is post-processing two different model variants.

ryan-ml: found server-side WARNING for the same timeframe: `model_variant_mismatch: client_expected_dim=1024, served_dim=768 for model redwood-embed-v1@rev:15` — that means routing returned a smaller-dim variant for some requests. It should not be common.

jess-product: if some requests route to a 768-dim variant, that would explain client-side mismatch but why slowdown? smaller-dim model should be faster.

marta-sre: slowdown likely from backpressure — I see fallback routing churn: requests were bounced between variants causing KV cache misses and extra recompiles. KV cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 72% during period. That plus GPU saturating explains vectors/sec drop.

sam-support: okay repro plan for customer: 1) run curl against embeddings endpoint with fixed model param `model=redwood-embed-v1:rev:15` and batch size 8 and 128, record p50/p95 and vectors/sec. 2) include header `X-Client-Dim:1024` (they currently send this). Can they do that?

carlos-cs: customer ran quick test — when pinning to `rev:15` small batch (8) p95 ~90ms per vector, big batch (128) p95 ~1.6s per vector. When omitting rev tag p95 ~2.1s per vector and occasionally dimension warning appears.

sam-support: thanks. that matches route churn theory. next: can eng-runtime provide counts for how many requests routed to each variant and whether autoscaler flapped around that time?

ryan-ml: pulling routing logs... counts: during incident window 03:10-03:30 UTC: rev:15 served ~62% of requests, rev:14 served ~36%, rev:beta (768-dim) served ~2%. but the issue is not just variant counts — it's the interleaving: many sessions started on rev:15 then got retried onto rev:14 due to transient capacity signal, then back. each switch invalidates per-host KV cache; cold-cache cost per request increased latency by ~300-400ms.

marta-sre: autoscaler noisy signal observed — GPU reclaim/resize events triggered because a host hit OOM on smaller batch allocation, leading to temporary capacity loss. I see a sequence of pod restarts around 03:11 that align with the initial queue surge. stack traces point to allocator: `cuda_out_of_memory` in one pod.

sam-support: that's actionable. immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pin customer's critical routes to a single variant (we can support route override) 2) temporarily reduce default max_batch for embed pool to avoid OOM thrashing 3) revert the pack_batch heuristic tweak from 2026.3.12 if it's root cause.

jess-product: product note: pinning model variants for single-tenant customers is allowed for Dedicated/Private, but for Hosted we need to ensure it's safe; we can create a per-tenant route policy to pin to rev:15 until we fix.

ryan-ml: also adding a quick repro script for eng to stress test and reproduce the queue churn locally:```
# repro stress script (pseudo)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v1","input": ["short text"] * 64}' &
done
wait
```

marta-sre: running that against a canary pool shows queue depth climbs and KV cache cold rate spikes when we force mixed variants. If we pin to a single variant the same load gives ~3x higher vectors/sec and no OOM.

sam-support: next steps for support: 1) propose temp route pin to customer and ask them to confirm latency improves 2) give them recommended batch size 8-16 for realtime and document that 128 is a heavy batch for hosted shared pools. 3) schedule eng rollback/patch.

carlos-cs: emailed Acme with the pin suggestion and recommended batching. they replied they can test tonight. they asked for an ETA on a permanent fix.

ryan-ml: eng plan: revert pack_batch tweak in 2026.3.12 (which changed batch packing to prefer larger micro-batches) and add an automated safety gate to detect increased KV cache miss and OOMs during a rollout. timeline: revert patch in next hotfix (EOD), run canary for 2 hours, then reintroduce improved heuristic behind a safer flag.

marta-sre: I'll also add an alert: if KV cache cold rate > 30% and GPU util > 90% and queue_depth > 30 for 5m -> page oncall.

sam-support: noted. I'll keep thread updated when Acme confirms. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.18-hotfix-packbatch-revert started by ryan-ml at 2026-03-18T18:04:12Z — canary pool: embed-pool-eu.

ryan-ml: canary looks good so far — vectors/sec returned to steady baseline on canary after revert (p95 improved from ~1.9s->210ms for batch=128 in pinned tests). rolling to remaining pools now.

carlos-cs: Acme tested pinned route and confirmed p95 dropped to ~200ms and no dimension warnings. they're happy with temp fix, asking for postmortem and timeline for permanent safe rollout.

sam-support: will prepare short postmortem draft with repro steps, root cause (pack_batch heuristic + routing churn + OOM causing autoscaler instability -> KV cache thrash -> backlog), customer impact, mitigation, and follow-ups (alerts, revert, safety gates, docs on batching guidance).

jess-product: add item to product backlog: clarify hosted batching recommendations and add per-route pinning option in Console for enterprise customers.

sam-support: closing loop here; leaving thread open for the postmortem doc link.

marta-sre: postmortem draft in #incidents will be linked once ready.
